content: Aluminum hydroxide is a medication prescribed to alleviate symptoms such as heartburn, sour stomach, and pain associated with peptic ulcers. It also aids in the healing of peptic ulcers. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. This medication is available in various forms, including capsules, tablets, oral liquids, and suspensions. The dosage and frequency of administration depend on the specific condition being treated. If you are using the suspension form, ensure that you shake it well before taking it. Always follow the instructions provided on the package or prescription label carefully. If you have any doubts or need clarification, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Aluminum hydroxide is sometimes used to reduce elevated phosphate levels in the blood of patients with kidney disease. If you are considering this medication for such a purpose, discuss the potential risks with your doctor. Before taking aluminum hydroxide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to it or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially if you are using drugs such as allopurinol, alprazolam, chlordiazepoxide, chloroquine, cimetidine, clonazepam, chlorazepate, dexamethasone, diazepam, diflunisal, digoxin, ethambutol, famotidine, halazepam, hydrocortisone, isoniazid, levothyroxine, lorazepam, methylprednisolone, oxazepam, penicillamine, prednisone, iron-containing products, tetracycline, ticlopidine, or vitamins. Aluminum hydroxide may interfere with the effectiveness of other medications. To avoid this, take other medications at least one hour before or two hours after taking aluminum hydroxide. Inform your doctor if you have a history of high blood pressure, heart disease, kidney disease, or gastrointestinal bleeding. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking aluminum hydroxide, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Aluminum hydroxide may cause side effects. Minor side effects include constipation and loss of appetite. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, such as confusion, unusual tiredness or discomfort, and muscle weakness, require immediate medical attention. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on the safe disposal of medications. Do not use aluminum hydroxide for more than two weeks unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
